windowNote: core = +30% within 14 days of report price (catalyst plays) · turbo = +50% within 30 days (moonshot plays) · MAE = max adverse excursion (worst drawdown before target hit, or over the window if never hit) · SOFT TARGETS (backlog #36): North Star hitRate currently reads 0% in EVERY bucket, so it cannot rank anything. softHitRate (+10% core / +20% turbo), medianExcessVsBenchPct and beatBenchRate are the metrics that discriminate — rank on those, and keep reporting hitRate as the honest scoreboard against the stated goal. · GUARDRAIL (2-tier, backlog #27): n < 5 in a bucket = context only, NEVER a reason to include/exclude/re-rank a pick. n >= 5 = MUST be applied — but do NOT re-derive this by eye: read `core.tier2`, which precomputes the eligible buckets, the laggards, and whether the rule fired. Screening output must state the tier2 verdict either way. · REGIME CAVEAT (both tiers): always read any rate next to avgBenchmarkPct/regimeNote — a 0% hit-rate measured in a deeply negative SPY window means "unproven in a bad regime", not "this type doesn't work". Check the actual regimeNote text each run; SPY does not see a sector-only selloff, a known gap in this rough v1 signal.

tier2.metricLabel: median (max gain − SPY over the same window), pp
tier2.note: Tier 2 FIRED. Picks whose primary catalystType is in `laggards` need visibly higher upside/conviction to make the top 5, and the screening output must name the type, its medianExcessVsBenchPct, and the overall figure. Ranking uses medianExcessVsBenchPct because the North Star hitRate reads 0 in every bucket and cannot discriminate. Still read each laggard's regimeNote before treating it as settled.

regime.note: SPY return over the same window as each complete entry (core+turbo combined). Pair with core.overall.regimeNote / core.byType[].regimeNote / turbo.overall.regimeNote before judging a hitRate — a low hitRate in a down-tape window is unproven, not disproven.

core.note: Measured reportDate → primary catalystDate + 3d, so the window CONTAINS the catalyst. Runs alongside the fixed 14d series, which is unchanged. medianPctAtAnchor = point-in-time return at window end (what you'd be holding just after the event); avgMaxGain = best point along the path. Entries with no explicit catalysts[].catalystDate are "undated" and excluded, not counted as misses. "no-data" means the cached price path stops before the catalyst — run npm run backtest:fetch to extend it. "beyond-cap" means the catalyst is further out than MAX_ANCHOR_WINDOW (120d) and is deliberately never fetched.

turbo.note: Measured reportDate → primary catalystDate + 3d, so the window CONTAINS the catalyst. Runs alongside the fixed 30d series, which is unchanged. medianPctAtAnchor = point-in-time return at window end (what you'd be holding just after the event); avgMaxGain = best point along the path. Entries with no explicit catalysts[].catalystDate are "undated" and excluded, not counted as misses. "no-data" means the cached price path stops before the catalyst — run npm run backtest:fetch to extend it. "beyond-cap" means the catalyst is further out than MAX_ANCHOR_WINDOW (120d) and is deliberately never fetched.

catalystAnchored.why: Added 2026-08-13 (backlog #38). /catalyst-list now accepts catalysts up to ~42 days out while the North Star measures 14d from report price, so a pick whose event is 4-6 weeks away is scored over a window that closes before the event and reads as a miss regardless of outcome (SRRK, catalyst 48d out, is the worked example). Read hitRate here NEXT TO core.overall.hitRate: if the fixed-window rate is ~0 but this one is materially higher, the fixed window is measuring the wrong thing for that pick, not measuring a bad pick.

core.note: optimismBias = written scenario % − realized max gain % over the same completed 14d window, core lane only. Positive = we write more optimistic scenarios than what actually happened. Do NOT compare this number across lanes — the bars differ by design.
core.horizonCaveat: HORIZON MISMATCH — read before acting on this. Realized figures are measured over the 14d North Star window, while a written Base/Bull scenario usually implies a longer horizon. So a positive optimismBias is NOT proof the scenario was wrong — it may just be a longer clock. That is why the rule below is "declare and justify", not "cap".
core.rule: Every core report must (a) state the measured optimismBias it was written against, and (b) if the written Base exceeds realizedMaxGainP75Pct, name the horizon that Base assumes and the specific driver that gets it there. A Base above realizedMaxGainP90Pct with no stated horizon is not acceptable — that is the failure mode this field exists to catch.

turbo.note: optimismBias = written scenario % − realized max gain % over the same completed 30d window, turbo lane only. Positive = we write more optimistic scenarios than what actually happened. Do NOT compare this number across lanes — the bars differ by design.
turbo.horizonCaveat: HORIZON MISMATCH — read before acting on this. Realized figures are measured over the 30d North Star window, while a written Base/Bull scenario usually implies a longer horizon. So a positive optimismBias is NOT proof the scenario was wrong — it may just be a longer clock. That is why the rule below is "declare and justify", not "cap".
turbo.rule: Every turbo report must (a) state the measured optimismBias it was written against, and (b) if the written Base exceeds realizedMaxGainP75Pct, name the horizon that Base assumes and the specific driver that gets it there. A Base above realizedMaxGainP90Pct with no stated horizon is not acceptable — that is the failure mode this field exists to catch.

scenarioCalibration.note: Split per lane on 2026-08-13 (backlog #39). Consumers MUST read scenarioCalibration.core or .turbo — there is deliberately no pooled top-level figure, because the previous pooled number mixed core and turbo Base scenarios (different bars) measured over 14d and 30d windows (different clocks) and was not usable by either lane.

stopGuidance.rule: entryStrategy.stopLoss.tight must sit WIDER than the relevant medianMAE (use core.byType[].medianMAE for the pick's catalystType when that bucket has n >= 5, otherwise core.overall.medianMAE / turbo.overall.medianMAE), or the report must say in one line why this specific setup justifies a tighter stop. Same number informs catalystSpot.stopPreCatalyst and spotSizing.
stopGuidance.caveat: MAE here is measured from the REPORT price, so it assumes entry at Entry 1 (now). A pick filled on the Entry 2 dip has a structurally shallower drawdown from its own fill — don't apply the full width mechanically to a dip entry.

core.note: Not perfectly apples-to-apples: near-miss uses point-in-time +14d price; picks use max gain within the 14d window (structurally favors picks). Treat edge as an upper bound, not exact.

turbo.note: Not perfectly apples-to-apples: near-miss uses point-in-time +30d price; picks use max gain within the 30d window (structurally favors picks). Treat edge as an upper bound, not exact.
